results: 1. Bedside neurological examination including true wrist and finger extension strength, pronator drift, tone, reflexes, sensation, coordination, and gait

coordination examination (limb and truncal): limb and truncal ataxia with action myoclonus
posture and pull test: impaired tandem stance and positive pull test

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Functional neurological symptom disorder (functional movement disorder causing apparent bilateral wrist drop), with no demonstrated structural, peripheral nerve, or metabolic cause

Alternative 1: Cerebellar ataxia with action myoclonus due to an autoimmune or paraneoplastic process

Alternative 2: Toxic or medication-induced cerebellar syndrome with myoclonus

Alternative 3: An inherited spinocerebellar ataxia syndrome
